exposure: Clinical pelvimetry parameters (sacral promontory, diagonal conjugate diameter, curvature of the sacrum, interspinous diameter, side walls, sacrosciatic notch, sub-pubic arch, prominence of coccyx, intertuberous diameter)
outcome: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 210 nulliparous women presenting for delivery.
finding: Neither clinical pelvimetry parameters nor trans-abdominal ultrasonography measurements of pelvic capacity were found to statistically predict the mode of delivery (vaginal vs. C/S) in nulliparous women.
mod_finding: The study concluded that clinical pelvimetry and sonopelvimetry were not effective in prognosing the mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section).
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken when nulliparous women presented for delivery.
